activity: Hands-on cooking classes (pasta and other cuisines)
how: CocuSocial and Classpop! run hands-on fresh-pasta and other cuisine classes at several metro locations, with ingredients supplied.
CocuSocial offers beginner sushi-rolling classes with no experience needed, and Classpop! runs Sushi 101 sessions at Chattahoochee Row.
Food halls such as Ponce City Market, Krog Street Market and Pine Street Market give a multi-stall, many-cuisine grazing experience, though not a hawker-centre culture.
venue: Ponce City Market Central Food Hall

how: H&F Whisk(e)y Society runs whiskey-focused tasting and education events in Atlanta.
Atlanta Whiskey Academy teaches an in-person Whiskey 101 class on history, production and tasting different styles.
Atlanta Wine School runs formal instructor-led wine classes including certification-style courses, and shops such as Highland Fine Wine and Barcelona Wine Bar host sommelier-led tastings.
Birds Georgia (formerly Atlanta Audubon) and Chattahoochee Nature Center host guided bird walks in metro parks and wetlands; Georgia Tech also runs a weekly birdwatchers club.
Chattahoochee Nature Center holds a seasonal Butterfly Encounter/festival with live butterflies, and its gardens attract wild butterflies.
Northlake Stamp & Coin, open since 1969, buys, sells and appraises coins alongside stamps and cards.
Northlake Stamp & Coin sells, buys and appraises stamps and collections.
Oxford Comics & Games (30+ years) and Titan Games & Comics are long-running comic shops in the metro area.
The Georgia Mineral Society in Norcross holds monthly meetings, fossil and mineral section meetings, workshops and regular field trips to collecting sites.
Premium Kicks is a sneaker resale boutique on Cheshire Bridge Road.
The Card Shop on Cheshire Bridge Road sells sports and trading cards, and Atlanta has many card shops across the metro.
Criminal Records in Little Five Points is a long-running independent shop selling new and used vinyl.
Atlanta History Center's Kenan Research Center and the Georgia Archives hold public research collections.
The High Museum of Art is the region's main art museum, with African, American and European collections.
Atlanta has major museums including the High Museum of Art, Fernbank Museum of Natural History and Atlanta History Center.
Fernbank Museum of Natural History has dinosaurs, fossils, live animals, a giant-screen theater and 75 acres of old-growth forest trails.
A weekly Sunday slam and open mic at Bar Crema in Decatur descends from the Java Monkey Speaks series, and the Art Amok! slam team runs a second venue.
Atlanta History Center hosts author talks, film screenings and public programs.

Atlanta Preservation Center offers volunteer-led 1.5-hour guided walking tours (Historic Downtown, Grant Park, Sweet Auburn, Inman Park) March to November; History Afoot Atlanta also runs neighborhood tours.
Atlanta Preservation Center's Sweet Auburn and Historic Downtown walking tours cover heritage districts, and the Atlanta History Center runs related tours.
Alliance Francaise d'Atlanta teaches French to adults and youth, with private and corporate classes and DELF/DALF preparation.
Atlanta Institute of Language teaches German in group and one-on-one classes.
Atlanta Institute of Language teaches Japanese in group and one-on-one classes.
Atlanta Institute of Language and Hyperfluent offer Spanish group and private lessons.
American Sign Language is taught at some metro colleges and community programs; no specific Atlanta provider confirmed.

Atlanta Humane Society takes volunteers for dog walking, fostering, shelter medicine help and outreach, with training at its Atlanta and Marietta locations; PAWS Atlanta in Decatur also needs volunteers.
Atlanta Humane Society and PAWS Atlanta run volunteer programs with orientations, including court-required service hours.
Atlanta Humane Society and PAWS Atlanta adopt out dogs and cats.
Piedmont Park lists dog parks among its amenities, with off-leash areas across the city.
Evolation Yoga, Yonder Yoga and Mysore Yoga Atlanta offer heated, vinyasa and Ashtanga classes.
Club Pilates offers small-group reformer classes and Evolation Yoga lists Pilates classes.
Perspire Sauna Studio (Pharr Road) and Refresh Cryo and Sauna sell infrared sauna sessions.
Refresh Cryo and Sauna offers contrast-therapy suites combining infrared sauna with cold plunge.
Body & Brain Yoga Tai Chi offers tai chi, qigong and meditation classes at Atlanta and Marietta locations.
Body & Brain Yoga Tai Chi teaches qigong with breathing and meditation.
Studios like Yonder Yoga and Mysore Yoga Atlanta, plus community and senior centers, offer guided meditation and breathwork.
Wellness and recovery studios such as Wellhaus and STAT Wellness offer massage and bodywork on ClassPass.
Atlanta Track Club, a large metro running club, hosts group runs and events.
Guided history and architecture walks along the BeltLine and in Grant Park and Old Fourth Ward offer sanctioned city exploration.
Treetop Quest Dunwoody has 60+ obstacles across four levels with a briefing; Level 4 is a difficult strength-and-balance course (ages 12+).
Treetop Quest Dunwoody's Level 3 course is all zip lines; Levels 1 and 2 suit beginners from age 7.
iFLY Atlanta, a vertical wind tunnel on Cobb Parkway, takes first-time flyers after a short briefing.
Wake the Lake Cable Park on Lake Lanier is described as the only cable wakeboard park in the metro area; the article is dated.
Atlanta-area gun clubs such as Atlanta Gun Club offer sporting clays and skeet shooting; not confirmed on an operator page.
Zoo Atlanta offers giraffe feeding, Wild Encounters and NightCrawler overnights as a safari-like experience.
Stone Mountain Park runs a seasonal artificial-snow tubing and play area in winter.
Atlanta is inland; whale and dolphin watching is on the Georgia/Florida coast around Savannah or Jacksonville, roughly 4-5 hours away, with right whales only in winter.
No sustained whitewater exists in the Piedmont metro; the Ocoee River on the Tennessee line, about 1.5 hours north, is the nearest commercial rafting (Raft One and others).
Atlanta's climate lacks reliable snow and elevation; the nearest ski resorts (Sugar Mountain, Beech Mountain) are in western North Carolina, about 4 hours away.
Dog sledding needs deep snow, which the Georgia Piedmont does not get; the nearest options are in the northern US or Canada, a flight away.
No glaciers exist in the Southeast; the nearest are in Alaska or the Rockies, a 4-5 hour flight away.
No volcanoes exist in Georgia; Cerro Negro in Nicaragua is the classic site, a few hours' flight away.
Georgia has no large desert dune fields; the nearest dunes are coastal sand dunes on the Georgia coast, about 4 hours away, and true desert is in the US Southwest.
Canyoning needs steep waterfall gorges, which the Piedmont lacks; the nearest guided canyoning is in the western North Carolina mountains, about 3-4 hours away.
Atlanta sits on crystalline Piedmont rock with no flooded cave systems; the nearest cave-diving springs are in north Florida, around 5-6 hours away.
The metro lies on non-karst Piedmont rock; the nearest accessible caves are in northwest Georgia limestone (e.g. Kingston Saltpeter Cave, Cloudland Canyon), roughly 1-1.5 hours away.
BASE jumping needs legal cliffs or fixed structures, which the metro lacks; the nearest recognised site is the New River Gorge Bridge in West Virginia (Bridge Day), around 7 hours away.
Bullfighting is outlawed or absent in Georgia; the nearest traditions are in Spain, Portugal or Mexico.
There are no alpine mountains in the metro; the Southern Appalachians of North Georgia and North Carolina, 1.5-4 hours away, offer hiking and rock climbing, and true mountaineering is in the Rockies.
